messages:
maya: Quick sync — launching a Community Quickstart Challenge the week of Apr 6 to drive OSS refapp adoption and capture inbound demo leads :rocket:
maya: Goals: 1) 1k signups to the starter repo, 2) 150 webinar registrants, 3) 30 qualified demo requests (SQL for SDRs)
jason: Love it. Do we have a benchmark narrative? e.g., local infer cost/latency comparisons to call out in the kickoff blog + slides
li: We do but it's rough. I can pull a short 3-bullet comparison: hosted vs dedicated vs private with a simple table for marketing copy. Need to know the target workloads (chat vs embeddings).
amanda: For the tutorial flow I propose 3 micro-tasks: 1) repo clone + run minimal local server, 2) switch model variant (quantized) and measure latency, 3) deploy to sandbox and call the /generate endpoint. Each should take <20 mins.
jason: Perfect — tutorial should include a small script to measure p99 and token cost. I can draft a code snippet for the README.
jason: ```bash
# quick p99 tester
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}' | jq '.latency'
```
maya: Webinar logistics: want 45 min hands-on + 15 min Q&A. Can we schedule Mon Apr 7 11am PT? @sam are you available to host demo ops? :calendar:
sam: Yup I'm free. I can run the live deploy step and field infra questions. Will also record a short failover demo if the model overloads.
amanda: Marketing assets checklist: blog post, tutorial repo (with issues for contributors), 3 short gifs for social, webinar landing page, email cadence (3 touches).
li: For messaging, keep it developer-first: "Ship an LLM-powered feature end-to-end in under an hour" and include explicit code + perf numbers. Don't overpromise SLA stuff.
maya: Draft copy for the blog intro — please review: 
```
Ship an LLM feature from code to live in under an hour. Join our Community Quickstart Challenge to get hands-on with a reference app, compare local vs hosted inference economics, and walk away with a working demo you can customize.
```
jason: Small suggestion: add a short benchmark callout near the top: "~3x cost reduction with our prefix caching + quantization tips (workload dependent)"
amanda: I'll turn that into an inline badge and GIF showing before/after latency.
bot-campaigns: campaign created: community-quickstart-challenge, landing page draft: https://redwood.example/challenge-draft (owner: maya)
maya: CTA: "Join the challenge" + calendar link. Proposed calendar: https://cal.com/redwood/quickstart-challenge-11am-PT
li: Can we add an optional pre-webinar lab: a short self-paced checklist so attendees can follow along? That reduces support during the live demo.
amanda: Yes — I'll add a "Prework" section in the landing page and a 5-step checklist in the repo README.
sam: SDR ask — in the form include a checkbox for "Interested in a dedicated capacity trial" so we can route leads into the right funnels. Also add a hidden utm param for channel attribution.
jason: For the tutorial repo, I'll add an issues template titled "Benchmark result" so community can submit their own measurements.
maya: Ok action items: maya -> blog & landing copy (by Thu), amanda -> social GIFs + email cadence (by Fri), jason -> tutorial + p99 script (by Thu), li -> benchmark bullets and slide deck (by Fri), sam -> webinar ops + lead form field (by Fri). We'll do a 20-min dry run Tue Apr 1 10am PT.
li: Dry run noted. I'll prep the slide with a single benchmark slide and a backup model variant for graceful degradation demo.
maya: Thanks team — let's keep thread updates here. Ping me if anything slips. :thumbsup:
